meta.description: Fast persistent serve mode for CLI

user.t:
Rust crate C:\Users\mariu\neural-mesh. Read DESIGN.md and src/main.rs (the `neural-mesh` CLI: route/feedback/stats, JSON out, state file with an exclusive .lock file and atomic writes). Toolchain: in every Bash call first run
export PATH="$HOME/.cargo/bin:/c/Users/mariu/AppData/Local/Microsoft/WinGet/Packages/BrechtSanders.WinLibs.POSIX.UCRT_Microsoft.Winget.Source_8wekyb3d8bbwe/mingw64/bin:$PATH"

Problem: each CLI call costs ~31 ms median (release) because of process start + full JSON state load/parse/save. Hooks call it on every prompt and howler may call it per task. Goal: make routing near-instant without breaking the existing CLI contract.

YOUR FILE: src/main.rs (you own it now) and new tests. Do NOT edit mesh.rs, hebbian.rs, variants.rs, sim.rs, stats.rs, memory.rs, bin/*.rs (other agents own them).
Implement:
1. `neural-mesh serve --state <file> [--port N | --stdio]`: a long-lived process that loads state once and answers JSON-lines requests {"cmd":"route"|"feedback"|"stats", ...same fields as the CLI flags} with the same JSON responses the CLI prints. `--stdio` mode (one request per line on stdin, one response per line on stdout) is required; a localhost TCP mode (127.0.0.1 only, never 0.0.0.0) is optional. Persist state with the existing lock+atomic write: write-behind (flush every N feedbacks or every T ms, and on shutdown/EOF) so a crash loses at most a bounded amount; document the bound. Concurrency rule: while a server holds the state, one-shot CLI calls must still be correct — use the lock file to coordinate (server takes the lock only while flushing, and reloads if the file's mtime changed since its last write), or document and test a simpler safe rule.
2. Keep all existing one-shot commands byte-compatible.
3. Measure: one-shot route latency vs stdio-server route latency (median/p90 over >=500 requests, release build), and feedback throughput. Target < 1 ms per request in server mode.
4. Tests: stdio request/response round-trip, malformed JSON line returns {"ok":false,...} and the server keeps running, write-behind flushes on EOF, a one-shot CLI call between server flushes does not lose either side's updates (or the documented rule holds).
cargo test --release green; clippy if available. Do not git commit. Report: protocol, flush/durability rule, latency numbers, test results.

resp.t: That notification is for a stray command I started by mistake early on. It was a Python heredoc probe that hung and was killed at its time limit. It had no effect on the work: the serve implementation, tests and benchmark were done independently, and my report stands as delivered. Nothing needs restarting.

handback.t:
`neural-mesh serve` is implemented and works. In stdio mode it answers about 100 us per route request, against 173 ms median for a one-shot call on this machine (not the 31 ms baseline; see Latency). `cargo test --release` is green: 90 lib tests, 5 main tests and 11 new serve tests. Clippy reports nothing for my files; the remaining warnings are in sim.rs, variants.rs and memory.rs, which are not mine.

Nothing is committed.

## Files
- **`src/main.rs` (edited)**
  - Added `mod serve;` and a `serve` dispatch at the top of `main()`.
  - `cmd_route` now validates all arguments before registering any agents. A failed route used to leave newly registered agents in memory, which the server would have kept. The one-shot CLI never saved on error, so its observable behaviour and error precedence are unchanged.
  - `USAGE` and the `--help` text are untouched, so one-shot output stays byte-compatible. `serve` has its own usage string.
- **`src/serve.rs` (new)** holds the server.
- **`tests/serve.rs`, `tests/common/mod.rs`, `tests/serve_bench.rs` (new)** hold the tests and the benchmark.
- I did not touch mesh.rs, hebbian.rs, variants.rs, sim.rs, stats.rs, memory.rs or bin/*.rs.

## Protocol
```
neural-mesh serve --state <file> (--stdio | --port N) [--flush-every N=64] [--flush-ms T=1000]
```
- **Framing:** one JSON object per line in, one per line out.
- **Requests:** `{"cmd":"route"|"feedback"|"stats", ...}`, with the same fields as the CLI flags minus `state`.
  - Values can be strings, numbers, or arrays for comma lists (`"candidates":["a","b"]`).
  - Null fields are ignored, and unknown fields are an error.
- **Responses:** the same object the CLI prints. They were equal in the parity test for route (with and without a seed), feedback and stats.
- **Extras:** an optional `"id"` is echoed back. `{"cmd":"flush"}` persists now and `{"cmd":"shutdown"}` persists, replies and exits.
- **Bad input:** a malformed line, a non-object, a missing or unknown `cmd`, a bad field, or invalid UTF-8 gets `{"ok":false,"error":"..."}` and the server keeps running. Blank lines are ignored with no reply.
- **TCP:** it binds 127.0.0.1 only, one thread per connection, and prints a banner `{"ok":true,"listening":"127.0.0.1:PORT"}` first. `--port 0` picks a free port.
- **Exit codes:** 1 for usage errors, 2 for I/O errors.

## Flush and durability rule
- **When it flushes:** state lives in memory. It is written with the existing lock file and atomic rename after `--flush-every` route or feedback requests, or `--flush-ms` after the first unflushed one. It also flushes on EOF and on `shutdown`. The timer is a ticker thread running every `flush_ms/4`, clamped to 5–250 ms.
- **Loss bound on a hard crash** (kill -9, power loss): at most `flush_every - 1` requests, or about 1.25 × `flush_ms` of mutations, whichever comes first. A clean EOF or `shutdown` loses nothing. SIGINT is not handled specially.
- **Coordination with one-shot CLI calls:**
  - **Normal operation:** the server holds the lock only while flushing. Before each request it compares the state file's (mtime, length) with what it recorded after its last read or write.
  - **External change:** it takes the lock, reloads the file and replays its journal of unflushed route and feedback requests on top, then writes the result. Both sides' updates survive.
  - **Ordering:** the merged order is "CLI call first, then the server's pending requests". Replies already sent for the pending requests were computed on the older base.
  - **Residual windows:**
    - A CLI call sees the server's updates only after the next flush, so its read can lag by up to the bounds above.
    - If a flush fails (for example the file was corrupted externally), the server logs to stderr and retries after one `flush_ms`, and the journal stays in memory.

## Latency
Release build on this machine, which was heavily loaded by other agents running at the same time. State: 8 agents, 400 feedbacks, 5.5 KB file. The server latencies are round trips including the pipe.

| Case | n | p50 | p90 | p99 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| One-shot `route` (process spawn) | 500 | 173 ms | 334 ms | 622 ms |
| stdio server `route` | 5000 | 95.6 us | 126 us | 1.58 ms |
| stdio server `feedback` | 5000 | 87.5 us | 114.8 us | 1.54 ms |

- The one-shot figure is far above the ~31 ms you measured because of the load, so treat it as a ceiling. The ratio is still more than 1000x at the median.
- Server feedback throughput was 8,463 requests per second.
- The p99 spikes come from the write-behind flush every 64 mutations. The maximum single request was 29 ms.
- Median and p90 are well under the 1 ms target. The p99 is slightly above it in this run because of the flushes. A larger `--flush-every` or `--flush-ms` moves them off the request path.
- To rerun the benchmark: `cargo test --release --test serve_bench -- --ignored --nocapture`.

## Tests (all pass)
The 11 serve tests in `tests/serve.rs`:
- stdio round trip, with parity against the one-shot CLI
- malformed lines, with the server staying alive and no state change on failed requests
- flush on EOF while write-behind holds state before it
- flush every N mutations
- flush after `flush_ms`
- `flush` and `shutdown` commands
- a CLI call between server flushes, with both sides' updates kept (feedback and update counts correct, no `.lock` left behind)
- a concurrent stress test of 25 CLI plus 60 server feedbacks, giving exactly 85
- TCP mode on localhost
- bad `serve` arguments
- one-shot output unchanged

Build note: `target/release/neural-mesh.exe` was locked by other agents' processes, so I built into `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=C:/Users/mariu/nm-target-serve`. The first build there took about 4.5 minutes.
